newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Recovering Yeltsin wants to leave heart clinic.
newsitem.headline: Recovering Yeltsin wants to leave heart clinic.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, in satisfactory condition after Tuesday's open heart surgery, is pressing the doctors to let him leave the specialist heart clinic for another hospital, the Kremlin said on Wednesday.
Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news conference that doctors had met on Wednesday and would meet again on Thursday to work out if the president could be moved.
"The president is chivvying the doctors (about the move) and he's keeping them on the defensive."
Yastrzhembsky said he believed psychological reasons were mainly behind Yeltsin's desire to return to the Central Clinical Hospital, where he has spent much time during previous illnesses.
Political analysts suggested a move to a less specialised hospital would also signal to the outside world that Yeltsin was on the road to recovery.
Yastrzhembsky said a council of doctors, including foreign experts, met on Wednesday to review Yeltsin's progress after Tuesday's seven-hour quintuple heart bypass.
"The patient's condition is stable, satisfactory, it corresponds to the gravity of the operation," he quoted their conclusions as saying.
Yeltsin's blood pressure and pulse were close to that of a healthy person but his temperature was higher than the norm which doctors said was "natural for such a serious operation".
"All of us in the Kremlin are in a good mood because Boris Nikolayevich is recovering quickly, surprising the doctors with his strong health and powerful will," he said.
